[SCENE GEOMETRY & ARCHITECTURE]
High-angle architectural documentary view looking down Marchmont Crescent at the intersection of Roseneath Street, Edinburgh, captured on 6x7 medium format camera, 45mm lens, f/8 aperture, fine-grain film, edge-to-edge optical resolution. Imposing 4-to-5-storey late-Victorian Scottish Baronial tenements constructed of solid Hailes blonde-grey and Locharbriggs pink sandstone snecked masonry. Prominent corner conical tourelles with corbelled ashlar bases, steep Scottish slate pitched roofs, crow-stepped wallhead gables, and heavy stone chimney stacks crowned with terracotta flue pots. Authentic historic carbon soot patination and rainwater wash marks tracing the ashlar dressings and roll-moulded window reveals. A completely deserted, decluttered asphalt intersection bordered by granite and whinstone kerb lines and traditional cast-iron railings, flanked by an organic green sycamore tree. Low-angle 3200K golden hour solar illumination raking across the stone facades from the northeast, casting crisp, elongated shadows along the street plane beneath a pristine clear sky.
